newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ultra-Orthodox Jews clash with police over street.
newsitem.headline: Ultra-Orthodox Jews clash with police over street.

text.p: Police and ultra-Orthodox Jews clashed on Sunday on a Jerusalem street that Israel's High Court ruled should be open to traffic on the sabbath, police and witnesses said.

The court ruling earlier on Sunday ended an unofficial eight-month truce along Bar-Ilan street and drew threats from a spokesman for the ultra-Orthodox community to renew weekly Saturday protests against the road being open.
Witnesses said several hundred religious Jews in traditional black garb gathered at Bar Ilan street on Sunday night to protest at the court ruling.

Police said some of the crowd hurled empty bottles and rocks at police from a side street but that there were no injuries. One protester was detained. Witnesses said protesters set one trash bin alight but traffic continued to flow.

Israel's Channel Two Television said that protection for High Court President Aharon Barak had been increased and that guards had been assigned to the other judges who signed Sunday's order. Police said the courts spokesman, who was not immediately available, would have to comment on the report.

Earlier in the day a courts spokesman said: "The transportation minister's decision to close the road was cancelled. The court ordered the issue back to the minister and that he take into consideration the interests of secular Jews who live on the street."

Secular lawmakers said the ruling to cancel last year's decision by Transportation Minister Yitzhak Levy, an Orthodox Jew, to close Bar-Ilan street during prayer times on the sabbath and Jewish holidays was a victory for democracy.
Ultra-Orthodox Jews had suspended their protests pending the court's decision on left-wing appeals against Levy's edict.

Orthodox spokesman Yehuda Meshi-Zahav told Israel's army radio:"The sabbath in history was governed by forces stronger than the High Court and it will triumph over the High Court. We will certainly continue with demonstrations."
Jewish ritual law forbids the operation of machinery, including vehicles, on the sabbath which runs from Friday night to Saturday night.
